name: User
rationale: A common authenticated actor supertype is needed for login, password, session, and role-based entry actions.
plain_english_summary: A person who can use iTrust after authenticating.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated user

name: User__mid
rationale: MID is the login identifier and appears as a patient field that must be protected from editing.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical identification number used to identify the account.
source_excerpt: Any user can enter their MID and password to gain role-based entry into iTrust.
alternatives_considered: Modeled MID only on Patient, but login applies to any user.

name: User__name
rationale: Name is used when initially creating patients and searching providers.
plain_english_summary: The person's name in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.
alternatives_considered: Duplicated name on Patient and Provider entities, but all actors are users.

name: User__email
rationale: Email is initially provided when an HCP creates a patient user.
plain_english_summary: The person's email address.
source_excerpt: Only the patient's name and email are initially provided by the HCP.

name: Patient
rationale: Patients are both principals and protected subjects/resources throughout the slice.
plain_english_summary: A patient whose account, records, provider list, and access logs are managed in iTrust.
source_excerpt: Important actors include HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, administrator, patient, personal representative, UAP, emergency responder, public health agent, and ordinary authenticated user.

name: Patient__providerList
rationale: Provider-list membership is central to patient viewing, adding, designating, and undesignating providers.
plain_english_summary: The list of providers associated with the patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Represented provider list only as a set of providers on Patient, but actions target the list as a resource.

name: Hcp
rationale: HCP is a role that can create patients and manage patient data subject to credential secrecy constraints.
plain_english_summary: A health care professional user.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create a patient and enter the patient as a new user of the system.

name: Lhcp
rationale: LHCP is a provider subtype created by administrators and designated by patients as DLHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health care professional in iTrust.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: Lhcp__specialty
rationale: The administrator must provide this field when creating a new LHCP and patients search by it.
plain_english_summary: The LHCP's medical specialty.
source_excerpt: The administrator must specify the specialty for a new LHCP.

name: Lhcp__hospitals
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to one or more hospitals.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals where the LHCP is assigned.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.
alternatives_considered: Modeled hospital assignment as a separate resource, but the slice only needs the relationship for assignment.

name: Lhcp__zipCode
rationale: Patients may search providers using zip code as an optional criterion.
plain_english_summary: The zip code associated with the provider for searching.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Put zip code only in action context search criteria, but provider matching needs a provider-side field.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrators create provider/public-safety accounts and configure inactivity periods.
plain_english_summary: An administrative user who manages users, hospitals, and system settings.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: Uap
rationale: UAP users are created by LHCPs and are an important actor type in the domain.
plain_english_summary: A user categorized as UAP in iTrust.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are account types created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A user who is an emergency responder.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are account types created by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A public health agency user.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, and public health agents.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representatives can view records for patients they represent.
plain_english_summary: A user authorized to act for one or more patients.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.

name: PersonalRepresentative__representedPatients
rationale: The represented-patient relationship must be explicit for record access decisions.
plain_english_summary: The patients for whom this user is a personal representative.
source_excerpt: for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Modeled the relationship only as action context, but it is reusable across multiple record-view actions.

name: Hospital
rationale: Hospitals are assigned to LHCPs by administrators.
plain_english_summary: A hospital that an LHCP can be assigned to.
source_excerpt: The administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals and choose the hospitals.

name: ProviderList
rationale: Provider lists are patient-owned resources updated by patients.
plain_english_summary: A patient's list of health care providers.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.

name: ProviderList__patient
rationale: Provider-list ownership is required for enforcing that patients change their own list.
plain_english_summary: The patient who owns the provider list.
source_excerpt: their provider list
alternatives_considered: Inferred from action name only, but ownership must be representable.

name: ProviderList__providers
rationale: The list must store HCP/LHCP providers that the patient adds or views.
plain_english_summary: The providers included in the patient's provider list.
source_excerpt: A patient can add a LHCP/HCP to their provider list by searching by name, specialty, and optionally zip code.
alternatives_considered: Used Set<Lhcp>, but the prose allows LHCP/HCP to be added.

name: ProviderDesignation
rationale: DLHCP is patient-specific, so the designation relationship should be modeled explicitly rather than as a global principal type.
plain_english_summary: A record that a patient designated a particular LHCP as DLHCP for that patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient and can undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: ProviderDesignation__patient
rationale: The designation applies to one specific patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient for whom the LHCP is designated.
source_excerpt: for that patient

name: ProviderDesignation__lhcp
rationale: The designation names the LHCP who is or may become a DLHCP.
plain_english_summary: The LHCP being designated or undesignated.
source_excerpt: any LHCP as a DLHCP

name: ProviderDesignation__isDesignated
rationale: Undesignation requires representing whether the patient-specific designation is active.
plain_english_summary: Whether this LHCP is currently designated as the patient's DLHCP.
source_excerpt: undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient
alternatives_considered: Deleting the designation entity, but an explicit Boolean supports both designate and undesignate actions.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records and their subcategories are protected resources for patients and representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record, including family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office visits.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative may view medical records including family history.

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Record ownership is needed for own-record and represented-patient access.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose information this medical record contains.
source_excerpt: their own records and for records of patients for whom the user is a personal representative

name: MedicalRecord__hasFamilyHistory
rationale: Family history is specifically included in medical-record viewing requirements.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record contains family history information.
source_excerpt: medical records including family history
alternatives_considered: Separate FamilyHistory entity, but the slice only requires viewing it as part of records.

name: MedicalRecord__hasPersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a specifically viewable category of medical-record data.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record includes personal health information.
source_excerpt: patient personal health information
alternatives_considered: Separate PersonalHealthInformation entity, but the slice treats it as record content.

name: MedicalRecord__hasImmunizations
rationale: Immunizations are a specifically viewable category of medical-record data.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record includes immunization information.
source_excerpt: immunizations
alternatives_considered: Separate Immunization entity, but the slice only needs to authorize viewing the category.

name: MedicalRecord__hasOfficeVisitInformation
rationale: Office-visit information is a specifically viewable category of medical-record data.
plain_english_summary: Whether the record includes office-visit information.
source_excerpt: office-visit information
alternatives_considered: Separate OfficeVisit entity, but the slice only needs record-level authorization.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Patient demographic data is an important resource and part of editable patient data.
plain_english_summary: Demographic details associated with a patient.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patients, personnel, medical records, demographic information, provider designations, access logs, sessions, credentials, and provider lists.

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic data belongs to a specific patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose demographic information this is.
source_excerpt: patient data
alternatives_considered: Put all demographic fields directly on Patient, but the spec names demographic information as a resource.

name: Credential
rationale: Passwords and security questions are protected credential resources with special secrecy constraints.
plain_english_summary: A user's password and security-question information.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.

name: Credential__user
rationale: Credential ownership is needed for password changes and patient credential secrecy.
plain_english_summary: The user account these credentials belong to.
source_excerpt: their password

name: Credential__hasPassword
rationale: Password is the credential used for login and password-change requests without exposing the secret value.
plain_english_summary: Whether the credential record contains a password secret.
source_excerpt: password
alternatives_considered: Stored password as String, but schema should not encourage exposing secret values.

name: Credential__hasSecurityQuestion
rationale: Security question is a protected credential element that HCPs must not access.
plain_english_summary: Whether the credential record contains a security question secret.
source_excerpt: security question
alternatives_considered: Stored securityQuestion as String, but access control only needs the protected field category.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Patients can view their own access logs over a selected period.
plain_english_summary: A log of accesses to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: A patient can view the patient's own access log.

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Access-log ownership is needed to restrict patients to their own logs.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: the patient's own access log

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: The access-log result must include the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the patient information.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessorRoleRelativeToPatient
rationale: The access-log result must include the accessor's role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: How the accessor is related to the patient for this access.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as an enum, but the spec does not list all possible values.

name: AccessLog__accessTimestamp
rationale: The access-log result must include when access occurred.
plain_english_summary: The time when the access happened.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: The access-log result must include the transaction type.
plain_english_summary: The kind of access or transaction that occurred.
source_excerpt: The access-log result contains the accessor name, the accessor role relative to the patient, the access timestamp, and the transaction type.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as an enum, but the spec does not list transaction types.

name: Session
rationale: A session entity represents the authentication boundary and inactivity termination condition for protected actions.
plain_english_summary: A user's logged-in iTrust session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__user
rationale: The active session must be tied to the authenticated requester.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the session.
source_excerpt: An authenticated session ends when the user logs out or closes the application.

name: Session__isActive
rationale: Authorization is disabled after logout, application close, or inactivity expiry, requiring an active-state field.
plain_english_summary: Whether this session is currently active.
source_excerpt: after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled

name: Session__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: Administrators can configure the inactivity period length.
plain_english_summary: The configured inactivity timeout for the session.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.
alternatives_considered: Created a separate system-settings entity, but the spec focuses on session inactivity behavior.

name: Session__lastActivityAt
rationale: Inactivity termination requires comparing the last activity time to the configured period.
plain_english_summary: The time of the most recent user activity in the session.
source_excerpt: Electronic sessions must terminate after the configured inactivity period; after the inactivity limit is exceeded, all authorization is disabled.
alternatives_considered: Used only isActive, but the configured inactivity period needs a time hook.

credentialField.rationale: The password/security-question restriction depends on the credential field.
